how_these_were_chosen: The resumption date as a plain integer with the generation index appended — 2026-08-12 run 01 and run 02. Same rule as specs/E09-seeds.json: the property that matters is that the number is fixed BEFORE any result is seen, and a date-derived seed is checkable against this file's own git timestamp. No seed here was drawn from a prior run, from any served template, or from anything this seat had already looked at.

ceiling.note: DERIVED 2026-09-03 from this file's own committed `allocation`, which names 2 entries: 2026081201 -> the diagnostic-donor generation A3.1 authorises; 2026081202 -> the reserve — A3 bounds this resumption at 2 generations total. The prose ceiling this key replaces did not exist in this file — the number is read off the allocation already committed here and is NOT a new authorisation. Spent credits have no compensator; the bound is the honest treatment.
ceiling.why_machine_readable: The value was free prose and no tool under tools/ read the key, while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated. CLAUDE.md makes the credit ceiling a per-spec obligation and records that spent credits have no compensator, so the one unrecoverable resource in this repo was bounded by a string nothing could parse. The prose is not deleted: it is `note`, verbatim, and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it. CORRECTION, 2026-09-04 (swarm wave 8, F-6c5c537b). This paragraph used to argue the fix with the clause “while `seeds` and `allocation` — its machine-readable siblings — are both consumed and gated”, and to close “and the number a submission step can count against sits beside it”. Both halves were measured on the tree and only one survived. `grep -rn allocation tools/ --include=*.py` returns 0 hits: `allocation` has no reader at all, so it is exactly as unread as `ceiling` was when it was filed. `seeds` has seven readers — build_animate_payload.py:475, build_camera_i2v_payload.py:1004, build_i2v_payload.py:496, build_lora_arm_payload.py:455, build_r2v_payload.py:207, build_t2v_payload.py:495 and gate_saved_graph.py:487 — each handing the list to a seed gate, so that half of the claim holds. And no tool reads `ceiling` from a seeds spec either: every `ceiling` hit under tools/ is `armature_core.assembly`'s unrelated CASCADE slot ceiling, or a builder passing that one. So `ceiling.submissions` is a number a submission step COULD count against and none does today — the bound is held by the spec and the executor, not by code. The original claim is kept above rather than deleted, because the correction is more useful than the original. tests/test_seeds_specs.py pins the measurement; the day a builder counts against `ceiling.submissions`, that test flips with it and this paragraph is rewritten again.

why_a_new_list_rather_than_the_old_reser: specs/E09-seeds.json registered 20260811 (spent on the probe) and 20260812 (its reserve). Reusing 20260812 here would put a seed registered for one trajectory onto a different one, and the record would then have to explain which run a number belonged to. A same-seed re-roll against the probe was considered and rejected on the measurement, not on tidiness: the prompt changes in this run too, so an identical noise draw would isolate nothing, and the two trajectories diverge from step 0 anyway (different shift, different step count).
binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces both clauses in code against the graph that is about to run, and ignores the inert seed of an add_noise=disable sampler because demanding registration there would be a check that fires on a correct two-expert split.
